html:
Tacky's Revolt was a rising of enslaved Africans in Jamaica in 1760, led by Tacky, a man of the Akan people of the Gold Coast. It was the biggest slave revolt in the British Caribbean in the 18th century.

The rebels, many of them Coromantee from what is now Ghana, rose at Easter in the parish of St Mary and later in the west. They aimed to drive out the British and set up an African state on the island.

The British, helped by the Maroons under the treaty of 1739, crushed it over months. Tacky was killed. Hundreds of rebels died and many were executed or shipped away. The revolt frightened planters across the empire and led to harsher laws, including bans on African religious practice.
sum: Tacky's Revolt was a rising of enslaved Africans in Jamaica in 1760, led by Tacky, a man of the Akan people of the Gold Coast. It was the biggest slave revolt in the British Caribbean in the 18th century.
